world.headline: Nepal flood death toll approaches 400 as more than 1,300 remain missing across the border region
world.body: Nepal police put the confirmed dead at 389 two days after a wall of water tore through Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading districts, with Chinese state media reporting further deaths and 558 missing on the Tibetan side. More than 700 of the missing are foreign nationals from two dozen countries, including 142 Indians and about 90 Americans. Nepali army helicopters pulled over 100 people out of the flood zone on Thursday and the Nepal Tourism Board says 27 foreigners have been rescued so far.

world.headline: Scientists trace the Nepal disaster to an ice and rock avalanche that dammed a Himalayan river
world.body: Researchers at ICIMOD and Nepal's disaster authority now attribute Wednesday's surge to an ice-rock avalanche that blocked the Lhende Khola before failing and releasing the water downstream, rather than to an earthquake. Satellite imagery reviewed alongside USGS analysis shows a large section of ice breaking away from a glacier above the valley. The finding pushes the event into the category of glacial hazards that are becoming more frequent as high-altitude ice destabilises.

world.headline: Kevin Warsh gives his first Jackson Hole speech as Fed chair with inflation still above target
world.body: Warsh takes the podium at the Kansas City Fed symposium on Friday morning US time, his most closely watched appearance since taking over the central bank. Inflation has reaccelerated through 2026 and the Fed has overshot its 2% target for six consecutive years, but Warsh has signalled he wants to address productivity, demographics and global shocks rather than the three remaining policy meetings. Bond markets are looking for any hint on whether he considers current inflation temporary.

world.headline: OpenAI, Anthropic and Google join more than 100 organisations warning on AI-enabled cyberattacks
world.body: The companies signed an open letter on Thursday alongside Microsoft and a group of financial services firms, arguing that businesses and governments are not prepared for hacking campaigns assisted by increasingly capable models. The letter frames defensive capability as lagging offensive capability and calls for coordinated action. It is one of the few instances of the major labs issuing a joint public position on security.

world.headline: Four EU states push Brussels to revive the Russian asset reparations loan for Ukraine
world.body: Sweden, the Netherlands, Spain and Poland circulated a draft dated 27 August asking EU foreign ministers to open discussion in Ireland on 1-2 September, eight months after Belgium blocked the plan on legal grounds. Kyiv faces a defence funding gap of about 23.1 billion euros, and the Council's own assessment is that the existing 90 billion euro interest-free loan covers only two-thirds of Ukraine's needs for 2026 and 2027. Belgium's objections have not changed.

world.headline: Qatar's prime minister visits Tehran as the Oman deal on the Strait of Hormuz stays unsigned
world.body: Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman al-Thani travelled to Iran to relaunch Doha's mediation track and discuss the wider regional file. A senior Iranian source told Reuters that the arrangement with Oman over the strait has not been finalised and that talks continue on the details, walking back the impression left by earlier statements this week. Shipping through the strait remains disrupted.

world.headline: CIA director travels to Moscow to warn Russia against action in the Baltic states
world.body: John Ratcliffe's trip carried a message that any attack on Estonia, Latvia or Lithuania would trigger a NATO response, alongside pressure on Moscow to cut back military and economic support for Iran. The visit comes after repeated Russian drone incursions into NATO and NATO-adjacent airspace, including into Romania and Moldova earlier this week. Moscow has given no public indication of a shift.

world.headline: Astronomers capture the clearest image yet of the companion star orbiting Betelgeuse
world.body: Observations with the SPHERE instrument on the European Southern Observatory's Very Large Telescope resolve Betelgeuse B, ending a search that began about a century ago when astronomers first proposed a companion to explain the red supergiant's periodic dimming. The data put the companion at two to three times the mass of the Sun, heavier than earlier estimates. Lead researcher Miguel Montarges of the Observatoire de Paris called it the conclusion of a century-long quest.

world.headline: Champions League draw sends Real Madrid to Arsenal and pairs PSG with Barcelona
world.body: The 2026-27 league phase draw at the Grimaldi Forum in Monaco set eight fixtures each for all 36 clubs, with holders Paris Saint-Germain drawn against Barcelona at home and Manchester City away. Real Madrid face Arsenal and Inter. The league phase runs from 8-10 September to 27 January, with the final in Madrid on 5 June 2027.

world.headline: Yayoi Kusama, Japan's queen of polka dots, dies at 97
world.body: The Yayoi Kusama Foundation announced on Thursday that the artist died of multiple organ failure at a Tokyo hospital on 14 August. Born in Matsumoto in 1929, she built a career out of the repeating nets and dots that came from childhood hallucinations, and her Infinity Mirror Rooms drew record museum queues worldwide. She had lived voluntarily at a Tokyo mental health hospital since 1977 and, the foundation said, painted until shortly before her death.

india.headline: 142 Indians listed among the missing in the Nepal flood as helplines stay open
india.body: Indian nationals form the largest single foreign contingent among the more than 700 foreigners unaccounted for after Wednesday's flood, most of them returning from Kailash Mansarovar pilgrimage routes through the Rasuwa crossing. The Indian embassy in Kathmandu has issued helpline numbers and India is among the countries that offered rescue assistance to Nepal, alongside China, the United States and the World Bank. Travel and trekking operators report 667 clients still out of contact.

india.headline: Sensex plunges 3% inside the closing auction before recovering to finish 539 points down
india.body: The benchmark fell about 3% during Thursday's 20-minute closing auction window and then clawed back nearly all of it, ending at 76,933.59, down 0.7%. The Nifty closed 116.90 points lower at 24,090.85 in a second straight losing session, dragged by metal, PSU bank and cement shares. The episode has renewed criticism of thin liquidity and the scope for manipulation in the auction window.

india.headline: US religious freedom panel asks Washington to sanction the RSS and revoke Mohan Bhagwat's visa
india.body: USCIRF said on Wednesday it was deeply concerned about the RSS chief's ongoing US visit, citing attacks on Christians, Dalits, Muslims and Sikhs, and chair Asif Mahmood urged targeted sanctions on RSS members and Indian officials. Bhagwat is scheduled to speak at an event in New York on Saturday. India's foreign ministry dismissed the commission's assertions and has previously described it as biased; USCIRF recommendations are advisory and have not been adopted by the State Department.

india.headline: Q1 GDP print lands on Monday with forecasts spread between 7.2% and 8%
india.body: The National Statistics Office releases first quarter FY27 estimates on 31 August. SBI Research projects close to 8% on broad-based momentum, while a Business Standard poll of economists sees growth easing to about 7.2% from 7.8% in the previous quarter on weak rains and softer services, and CareEdge puts it at 7.3%. The RBI held the repo rate at 5.25% on 5 August and raised its full-year growth projection to 6.7%.

india.headline: More than 43 lakh Karnataka voters to receive notices under the special intensive revision
india.body: The state chief electoral officer's draft roll carries 4,46,35,975 electors, and the next phase requires over 43 lakh of them to respond to verification notices. Claims and objections run from 24 August to 23 September, with the final roll due on 27 October. The draft follows house-to-house enumeration by booth level officers between 30 June and 17 August.

india.headline: Dassault submits its bid for 114 Rafale fighters under the multi-role aircraft tender
india.body: The French proposal offers 20 aircraft delivered flyaway from France and 94 built in India, at a figure reported at roughly Rs 3.25 trillion, with extensive local production content. The offer is under review by the Indian side and is not a signed contract. It arrives days after Rajnath Singh approved transferring DRDO's conventional missile technologies to domestic industry.

india.headline: Indian AI startups have raised $1.34 billion across 66 rounds so far in 2026
india.body: Funding is up 143% on the same period last year, with $676 million of it landing in the first half against $162 million across 30 deals in H1 2025. About two-thirds of institutional investors surveyed said the IndiaAI Mission, with an outlay above Rs 10,372 crore and 4,096 H100 GPUs allocated, shaped their investment thesis. India now counts more than 4,500 active AI startups, third behind the United States and China.

india.headline: DNA from an 1836 museum specimen confirms a distinct Himalayan pangolin species
india.body: Researchers sequenced the type specimen held at the Natural History Museum in London and matched it to modern animals from Nepal, northern India, Bhutan and Myanmar, establishing Manis aurita as a species separate from the Chinese pangolin. The result also renames the population described in 2025 as Manis indoburmanica. Being able to identify the species from scales gives enforcement agencies a way to trace seized shipments back to the region they were poached from.

india.headline: IMD puts nine Kerala districts on orange alert with heavy rain forecast across the north and east
india.body: The forecast for Friday warns of isolated very heavy rainfall of 115.6mm to 204.4mm in 24 hours over parts of Kerala, with heavy falls also expected in south Bengal, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Uttar Pradesh. The department expects active monsoon conditions across northwest, central and east India, including Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand and Odisha, through early September.

india.headline: Dinusha's unbeaten 133 earns Sri Lanka a draw in Colombo but India take the series 1-0
india.body: Sonal Dinusha faced 426 balls across the match, following a first-innings 103 with 133 not out to see Sri Lanka to 429 for 9 in reply to India's 503 for 9 declared and 290 first up. He was named player of the match. Devdutt Padikkal took the player of the series award with 328 runs, including centuries in both Tests.
